healthcare.quote: A story from our news operation about patients getting caught up in errors in Medicaid computer systems, operated by a private contractor. This is a symptom of a health insurance system that has become mind-numbingly complex.

I see lots of mentions of the cost of Medicare for All. But, it wouldn't necessarily increase health spending, and could actually decrease it. What it would do -- which would be controversial -- is redistribute health care spending from premiums and out-of-pocket costs to taxes.

Why is there a whole lot more talk about drug prices than hospital prices?

Paraphrasing bank robber Willie Sutton: If we want to restrain health spending, we have to go where the money is -- hospitals.
